messages:
ara_docs: Quick PR to add a short troubleshooting section for "fallback latency" in the Dedicated provisioning guide. Explains where to check prefix cache state and what logs to surface. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/968
tom_runtime: important to show the right logs. Recommend referencing runtime/kvcache state and the orchestration events stream.
sasha_pm: customers keep asking why latency spikes on fallback are higher than expected; can we add an example timeline? Could be helpful in the troubleshooting flow.
mike_sre: added a concise timeline example in the PR: 
- t0: tenant request routed to reserved pool node A (cache hit)
- t1: node A drained for maintenance -> cache eviction
- t2: request routed to variant B in shared pool (cold cache) -> added 200-1500ms encode cost
- t3: warmed cache after 3-5 requests -> latency returns to baseline

ara_docs: thanks! I also added a snippet showing the control plane API to check cache status:

```http
GET /v1/tenants/acme/cache-status
Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN

# response fields: { "has_prefix_cache": true, "last_evicted": "2026-02-12T15:03:21Z" }
```

docs-bot: lint: HTTP snippet uses example response; make sure to mark it as illustrative.
ara_docs: updated comment.
tom_runtime: small note: response field "has_prefix_cache" is only available on Dedicated registries; add a note for Hosted variants.
ara_docs: added note. PR merged by ara_docs.
ara_docs: will also add a short link to the SLA wording about maintenance windows."
